mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-16.1 to -12.1), indicating a sustained recovery trend driven by gradual resumption of discretionary outings. This momentum is expected to continue, pushing the next-4-week mean above the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days falls below the mean of the last 28 days despite the four-week rising streak.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility jumped sharply from -14.7 to -10.7 in the most recent week, suggesting households are increasingly willing to leave home for outdoor leisure. This behavioral loosening is expected to spill over into retail and recreation visits within one week as general outing propensity rises.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -14.7 to -10.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS jump exceeding 3 points, or declines instead.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed near -20 points with no sustained recovery, indicating continued suppression of out-of-home trip-taking infrastructure. If TRANSIT fails to improve by more than 2 points over two weeks, RETAIL_REC recovery will stall or reverse because transit access is a necessary precondition for retail visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT fails to improve by more than 2 points over the prior two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT remaining flat or stagnant.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed persistently elevated around 11-12 points with no downward movement, indicating households still spend disproportionate time at home. Combined with a WORKPLACES mobility that remains deeply negative (around -9 to -11), this interaction signals that people are not resuming office-anchored routines that typically generate adjacent retail trips, capping any retail rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable near 11-12 while WORKPLACES stays near -9 to -11
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even though both RESIDENTIAL stays above 11 and WORKPLACES stays below -8.

mechanism_narrative: If Singapore enters a tightening phase of restrictions (signaled by a simultaneous sharp drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT of more than 5 points within one week), RETAIL_REC will fall sharply within the following week as discretionary movement is curtailed by policy.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both drop more than 5 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:no such simultaneous drop observed in the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a simultaneous drop of more than 5 points in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has turned positive and stable (0.1 to 3.6), reflecting normalized essential-trip behavior. Because grocery and retail trips are often bundled in the same outing in Singapore's mall-centric commercial layout, continued GROCERY_PHARM stability above zero will support a modest rise in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 0.1 to 3.6 and stayed positive for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable and positive.

mechanism_narrative: The decision point falls in mid-March, prior to any major Singapore holiday period; absent a seasonal demand shock, RETAIL_REC is expected to continue its recent gradual linear improvement trend over the next 4 weeks consistent with the observed slope of approximately +1.3 points per week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved by about 1.3 points per week on average over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: The average weekly change in RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks drops below zero, breaking the extrapolated linear trend.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility rebounds sharply above -5 points (indicating eased workplace restrictions) while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously falls below 10 points (indicating reduced stay-home behavior), this joint regime shift toward reopening will trigger a pronounced increase in RETAIL_REC within four weeks as commuting and discretionary outings both normalize together.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -5 and RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 within the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES currently at -9.7 and RESIDENTIAL at 11.4, neither condition yet met
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even after WORKPLACES exceeds -5 and RESIDENTIAL drops below 10 in the same week.
